title: Market Design
tagline: Auction formats, revenue equivalence, optimal auctions, common values and the winner’s curse, multi-unit and spectrum auctions, stable matching, school choice and kidney exchange
summary: Some markets are designed rather than grown: auctions for radio spectrum and government bonds, clearing houses for junior doctors, school admissions and kidney exchanges. This course develops auction theory — the standard formats, revenue equivalence, optimal auctions, common values and multi-unit auctions — and matching theory — stable matching, the deferred-acceptance algorithm, school choice and exchange without money — and shows how both have been used to design real markets.

chapters.title: Auction formats and private values
chapters.summary: English, Dutch, first-price and second-price auctions, and equilibrium bidding with independent private values.

chapters.title: Revenue equivalence
chapters.summary: The revenue equivalence theorem, its assumptions, and how risk aversion, asymmetries and budget constraints break it.

chapters.title: Optimal auctions
chapters.summary: Myerson’s optimal auction, virtual values and reserve prices.

chapters.title: Common values and the winner’s curse
chapters.summary: Interdependent values, the winner’s curse, affiliation and the linkage principle.

chapters.title: Multi-unit and spectrum auctions
chapters.summary: Uniform-price and discriminatory auctions, demand reduction, and simultaneous ascending and combinatorial auctions.

chapters.title: Stable matching
chapters.summary: Two-sided matching markets, the Gale–Shapley deferred-acceptance algorithm and the structure of stable matchings.

chapters.title: School choice and the medical match
chapters.summary: Strategy-proofness, the Boston mechanism versus deferred acceptance, and the redesign of the US medical residency match.

chapters.title: Exchange without money
chapters.summary: Housing markets, the top trading cycles algorithm and kidney exchange.
